title: PM-MCP model verification item
description: One verification task for a model role: what the model sees (input), the reference answer (target), how an answer is graded, where the case comes from, who reviewed the reference, and contamination notes. Field names follow the sample model of Inspect AI (id, input, target, choices, metadata) where they overlap. Results are never stored in an item.

id.description: <topic path>/<slug>; equals the file path below the corpus root without .json

role.description: the configured role that answers the item (doc/concepts/harness-as-worker/roles.adoc#configuration)

group.description: items that share one case (for example the split and combined forms of a self-review)

facts.description: exactly the text the model sees besides the question; complete repository-relative paths

answer_schema.description: the JSON Schema of an open answer

context.description: corpus files the answering role must have besides question and facts (for example a project skill whose rule the answer follows), relative to the corpus root

answer.description: a choice, a label, or the expected action of an open answer

items.description: rubric items an open answer must meet: seeded defects or essential properties

location.description: file:line in the new code, where it applies

applies_to.description: which questions of a split review the item belongs to

expected_empty.description: a control: the correct answer reports nothing

method.description: exact_choice and label compare the answer with target.answer; rubric_items scores the share of target.items found (a control scores 1 only when empty); rubric_properties scores the share of target.items met; execution runs the answer code without network in a confined job and passes when every test passes

judge.description: the judge instruction or model, for rubric methods

kind.description: imported items are generated from a pinned public source; their origin names the source repository, its commit, the row, and the SPDX license id

commit.description: the commit the case concerns; for imported items the pinned source commit

url.description: a lasting URL of the source (a review comment, an issue)

record.description: citation of a non-public record the case was taken from (a plan's log entry), with the plan's name; the record itself is not retained

row.description: source row identifier for imported items (for example HumanEvalComm task_id with variant, or the BouncerBench instance id)

license.description: SPDX license id of the source for imported items (for example Apache-2.0, MIT, CC-BY-4.0); required when provenance.kind is imported

url.description: a lasting URL of the source (a review comment, an issue)

record.description: citation of a non-public record the case was taken from (a plan's log entry), with the plan's name; the record itself is not retained

based_on.description: for hand-made cases: the real code they were written against

history.description: how the item came about and changed, dated, in words that stay meaningful without any tool or plan of the time

contamination.description: what in this or another item gives the answer away, and which items must not share a session

canary.description: the corpus canary GUID; a model that reproduces it has seen the corpus
